conflicts: 4p 4S°3/2 lifetime: measured 36.9(1.8) ns (Berzinsh et al. 1997) vs their own relativistic Hartree-Fock 22.0 ns and MCHF 27.8 ns; the authors flag this level as the one clear disagreement (strong cancellation in the 4s 4P - 4p 4S° radial integral).

4s 4P lifetime: 4.0(0.5) ns measured for the multiplet (Savage & Lawrence 1966; their multiplet A = 2.50e8 s^-1) vs ab initio MCHF 4.9-5.0 ns; NIST ASD A-values (2.13-2.17e8 s^-1, accuracy 25 %) correspond to 4.6-4.7 ns.

3s3p4 4P levels: the ab initio MCHF table gives lifetimes of 1.6-2.8 microseconds, whereas the NIST ASD A-values of the 167 nm lines (3.9-4.0e7 s^-1, accuracy 50 %) imply about 25 ns; the theory value is not used here.

Relative strengths within 3p3 4S° - 3s3p4 4P: Mazzoni & Ricci 1996 measure I(1679.7):I(1674.6):I(1671.7) = 0.534:0.277:0.189, i.e. the J=5/2 and J=3/2 lines in the ratio 1.93 rather than the 1.46 expected from the NIST (Wiese & Martin 1980) gA values; the 1671.7 A line is blended.
not_found: beam-foil lifetimes of the 4s 4P, 4s 2P, 4s' 2D and 3s3p4 4P levels (Curtis, Martinson, Buchta, Phys. Scr. 3, 197 (1971); Livingston, Kernahan, Irwin, Pinnington, Phys. Scr. 12, 223 (1975)): papers not accessible, no open source quoting the numbers was found; only the 1966 phase-shift multiplet lifetimes are given
lifetimes of 3s3p4 4P5/2,3/2,1/2 (59534.549, 59715.921, 59820.371 cm^-1): no measurement opened; theory unreliable (see conflicts)
lifetimes of 4p 4D°1/2 and 4p 4P°1/2: not measured (Berzinsh et al. measured J=3/2 of each term); relativistic Hartree-Fock values given and marked theory
measured lifetimes or forbidden-line A-values of the metastable 3p3 2D° and 2P° levels: none located; lifetimes given are derived from the calculated A-values already in NIST ASD
measured Lande g factor of the 4S°3/2 ground level and hyperfine data of Pendlebury & Smith, Proc. Phys. Soc. 84, 849 (1964): paper not accessible
hyperfine constants of the 2D°, 2P° metastable levels or of any excited level of 31P: no measurement located
isotope shifts: not applicable (31P is the only stable isotope)
precise (laser) transition frequencies of P I lines beyond the NIST level energies: none located
laser-cooling or precision-spectroscopy use of P I lines: none located apart from the remark of Lee & Fairbank (2010) that the 177 nm resonance transition is too far in the VUV
notes: Level energies are the NIST ASD values (data/nist/P_I_levels.tsv); Berzinsh et al. print slightly different energies (e.g. 66813.04 for 4p 2D°3/2, NIST 66813.271). Savage & Lawrence lifetimes are multiplet values and are attached to every fine-structure level of the upper term. Berzinsh error bars are two standard deviations. Their two-photon excitation wavelengths were 299-306 nm (from 3p3 4S°3/2), detection on the 178 nm (quartets) or 214 nm (doublet) cascade. The lifetimes of the metastable 2D° and 2P° levels are derived from calculated A-values (theory). Note for the site: for the forbidden lines NIST lists separate M1 and E2 A-values at the same wavelength (e.g. 533.39 nm: M1 1.08e-1, E2 3.3e-7 s^-1); both must be summed for the decay rate. 'multiplet_intensity_fraction' is a non-schema field holding the measured relative line intensities of Mazzoni & Ricci.
